item.title: ‘Love Is Blind’ Season 10 Is Not-So-Subtly Superficial
item.description: After 10 seasons, it seems that a marriage success rate of 5 percent should be enough to reject the show’s hypothesis. Despite this, hosts Nick and Vanessa Lachey continue to give new contestants the not-so-promising chance to find love—this time in Ohio.

item.title: Newton Economic Development Commission Introduces Database to Map Vacant Storefronts and Attract New Businesses
item.description: Newton’s Economic Development Commission met on Tuesday evening to introduce a new digital map that locates vacant storefronts across the city’s thirteen village centers, hoping to update the technology available in Newton and attract new business. Lauren Berman, director of economic development, and Cheryl Lappin, deputy director of economic development, presented on the database project...

item.title: BC Falls Behind Early, Loses 85–76 to Florida State for 19th Straight Loss
item.description: Boston College women's basketball could not overcome an early 16–0 run from Florida State on Thursday night as the Eagles dropped their 19th straight game.

item.title: Karley and Taiga Guterres Connect Love and Faith in Valentine’s Day Agape Latte Talk
item.description: Students came together, coffees in hand, on Tuesday evening to hear Karley and Taiga Guterres share their connection with faith and each other.

item.title: ‘Katt Williams: The Last Report’: Conspiracies, Celebrities, and the Current Climate
item.description: Williams frames himself as a secular saint, an informant who has spent years infiltrating the halls of Hollywood just to bring the report back to us—it’s a brilliant framing device.

item.title: How Galentine’s Was Written Into Existence
item.description: Leslie Knope, the female lead played by Amy Poehler, made a practical joke that ultimately created the holiday we now know as Galentine’s Day. In typical Leslie fashion, the idea of “kicking it with the girls” was intended as a joke, but sixteen years later, Galentine’s is somehow still a thing.

item.title: Feminism on Feb. 14th: Five Films That Feature Female Friendships
item.description: In the spirit of Galentine’s, I want to highlight some movies that instill a sense of appreciation for the women in my life. So, without further ado, here are some film picks that revolve around powerful female friendships.

item.title: Campus Connections: Five BC Faculty Couples’ Love Stories
item.description: The person who stands at the chalkboard proctoring tests with a menacing gaze couldn’t possibly be the same person who returns to their spouse and family at the end of each day—or could they? The Heights spoke to five married couples who work at Boston College. Here’s what they had to say.

item.title: UGBC Releases Statement Addressing ICE After Months of Pressure
item.description: UGBC affirmed its solidarity with immigrant and international students amid “violent behavior” from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in a statement Thursday morning that followed months of student pressure.
